examInfo.title: CTFL - V4.0 - EN - SAMPLE EXAM - MODEL C

questions.questionText: Which of the following BEST explains why testing is necessary in software development?

options.label: a
options.text: Because developers always write incorrect code

options.label: b
options.text: Because software systems may have defects that can cause harm to people, organizations, or the environment

options.label: c
options.text: Because regulatory agencies require testing for all types of software

options.label: d
options.text: Because automated tools can replace the development process

a.explanation: Developers do not always write incorrect code; human error is natural but not universal.

b.explanation: Software systems can contain defects that, if not detected, may cause significant harm to people, organizations, and the environment — this is the fundamental reason testing is necessary.

c.explanation: Regulatory requirements apply only to certain domains; testing is necessary more broadly than just for regulatory compliance.

d.explanation: Testing tools support but do not replace the development process.

questions.questionText: The principle 'early testing saves time and money' means:

options.label: a
options.text: Testing should only be performed in the early stages of a project

options.label: b
options.text: Defects found and fixed early in the SDLC cost significantly less than defects found and fixed later

options.label: c
options.text: Automated tests should be written before manual tests

options.label: d
options.text: Test planning should be completed before the project starts

a.explanation: The principle recommends starting testing early, but does not mean it should only occur early.

b.explanation: The cost to fix a defect increases exponentially the later it is found in the SDLC. Fixing a requirements defect before code is written is far cheaper than fixing it in production.

c.explanation: The order of automated vs manual tests is unrelated to this principle.

d.explanation: While early test planning is good practice, the principle specifically refers to the cost of defect discovery and correction.

questions.questionText: Which of the following scenarios illustrates the testing principle 'testing is context-dependent'?

options.label: a
options.text: A tester applies the same regression test suite to every project

options.label: b
options.text: A safety-critical medical device system undergoes much more rigorous testing than a mobile game app

options.label: c
options.text: Testing always follows the same phases regardless of the project type

options.label: d
options.text: All defects are treated with the same priority regardless of severity

a.explanation: Applying the same regression suite to every project violates context-dependence.

b.explanation: Testing rigor, approach, and techniques differ based on context. A medical device with patient safety implications requires far more rigorous testing than a casual game.

c.explanation: Test phases and emphasis vary by context; not all projects follow the same test phases.

d.explanation: Treating all defects equally regardless of severity is inappropriate and unrelated to this principle.

questions.questionText: Which of the following BEST describes the test EXECUTION activity?

options.label: a
options.text: Defining test conditions and high-level test cases

options.label: b
options.text: Running the tests, comparing actual results to expected results, and logging outcomes

options.label: c
options.text: Preparing test environment and test data

options.label: d
options.text: Reviewing the test basis for testability

a.explanation: Defining test conditions is part of test analysis.

b.explanation: Test execution involves running the prepared tests, comparing actual outcomes to expected results, and logging the outcomes as pass, fail, or blocked.

c.explanation: Preparing test environment and data is part of test implementation.

d.explanation: Reviewing the test basis for testability is part of test analysis.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statements about test completion is CORRECT?

options.label: a
options.text: Test completion happens only once at the very end of a project

options.label: b
options.text: Test completion involves archiving testware and producing a test completion report

options.label: c
options.text: Test completion starts at the same time as test planning

options.label: d
options.text: Test completion eliminates the need for future testing of the same product

a.explanation: Test completion happens at the end of each test level or major milestone, not just at the very end of a project.

b.explanation: Test completion activities include archiving testware for future use, producing a test completion report, and ensuring lessons learned are documented.

c.explanation: Test completion occurs after test execution, not at the same time as planning.

d.explanation: Completing a test cycle does not eliminate future testing needs; the product will require maintenance testing.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an example of a false positive in testing?

options.label: a
options.text: A defect that exists in the code but is not detected by any test

options.label: b
options.text: A test that passes even though the feature is broken

options.label: c
options.text: A test that fails even though the feature works correctly

options.label: d
options.text: A test that is never executed during the test cycle

a.explanation: A defect that escapes detection is a false negative (the test did not catch the defect).

b.explanation: A passing test when the feature is broken is a false negative.

c.explanation: A false positive occurs when a test reports a failure, but the feature actually works correctly. This wastes time investigating non-existent defects.

d.explanation: An unexecuted test is simply a missed test, not a false positive.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a task typically performed by a TESTER (not the test manager)?

options.label: a
options.text: Deciding the overall testing strategy

options.label: b
options.text: Allocating the testing budget

options.label: c
options.text: Designing and executing test cases

options.label: d
options.text: Negotiating testing scope with project stakeholders

a.explanation: The overall testing strategy is defined by the test manager, not individual testers.

b.explanation: Budget allocation is a management responsibility.

c.explanation: Individual testers are primarily responsible for designing and executing test cases, reporting defects, and documenting test results.

d.explanation: Negotiating scope with stakeholders is typically done by the test manager.

questions.questionText: What is the relationship between quality assurance (QA) and testing?

options.label: a
options.text: QA and testing are identical activities

options.label: b
options.text: QA focuses on process; testing is one part of QA focused on product quality

options.label: c
options.text: Testing replaces QA in modern Agile development

options.label: d
options.text: QA is performed only by dedicated QA teams, while testing is done by developers

a.explanation: QA and testing are related but distinct. QA is broader than testing.

b.explanation: Quality assurance is a process-focused activity ensuring quality is built in throughout the SDLC. Testing is a product-focused activity and one part of the overall QA approach.

c.explanation: Agile still includes both QA processes and testing activities.

d.explanation: Both QA and testing can be performed by various team members; it is not restricted to specific roles.

questions.questionText: Which of the following BEST describes how Agile teams typically manage test documentation?

options.label: a
options.text: Agile teams produce extensive formal test documentation for every sprint

options.label: b
options.text: Agile teams use lightweight documentation such as user stories with acceptance criteria instead of formal test plans

options.label: c
options.text: Agile teams do not produce any test documentation

options.label: d
options.text: Agile teams produce the same documentation as waterfall projects

a.explanation: Agile values working software over comprehensive documentation and prefers lightweight artifacts.

b.explanation: Agile teams favor lightweight documentation such as user stories with acceptance criteria, test charters, and automated test results rather than traditional formal test plans and specifications.

c.explanation: Agile teams do produce documentation; it is simply lighter than in traditional projects.

d.explanation: Agile documentation practices are significantly lighter than in waterfall projects.

questions.questionText: Which of the following BEST describes the purpose of system integration testing?

options.label: a
options.text: Testing individual functions within a single software component

options.label: b
options.text: Testing the interfaces between the system and external systems or services

options.label: c
options.text: Confirming that defects from previous test cycles have been fixed

options.label: d
options.text: Testing whether the system meets contractual or regulatory requirements

a.explanation: Testing individual functions within a component is component (unit) testing.

b.explanation: System integration testing focuses on the interactions between the system under test and external systems, third-party software, or hardware interfaces.

c.explanation: Confirming fixed defects is confirmation testing.

d.explanation: Testing against contractual or regulatory requirements is a form of acceptance testing.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a type of NON-FUNCTIONAL testing?

options.label: a
options.text: Testing that a login form accepts valid credentials

options.label: b
options.text: Testing how the system behaves under peak load

options.label: c
options.text: Testing that a newly reported defect has been fixed

options.label: d
options.text: Testing that an e-commerce cart correctly calculates totals

a.explanation: Testing valid credentials is functional testing — it tests what the system does.

b.explanation: Load testing under peak conditions is non-functional testing. It tests how well the system performs (quality characteristics), not what it does.

c.explanation: Testing a fixed defect is confirmation testing, a type of change-related testing.

d.explanation: Cart total calculation is functional testing.

questions.questionText: What is the MAIN reason regression testing is often automated?

options.label: a
options.text: Automated regression tests are easier to write than manual tests

options.label: b
options.text: Regression testing involves repeating the same tests frequently, which is well suited to automation

options.label: c
options.text: Regulatory requirements mandate automated regression testing

options.label: d
options.text: Automated regression tests always find more defects than manual regression tests

a.explanation: Automated tests are not necessarily easier to write; they require significant initial effort.

b.explanation: Regression tests are executed repeatedly after every change. This repetitive nature makes them ideal candidates for automation to save time and ensure consistency.

c.explanation: Regulatory requirements do not universally mandate regression test automation.

d.explanation: The advantage is consistency and speed, not necessarily finding more defects.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is TRUE about maintenance testing scope compared to initial development testing?

options.label: a
options.text: Maintenance testing always covers the same scope as the original system test

options.label: b
options.text: Maintenance testing scope is typically smaller and is based on impact analysis of the change

options.label: c
options.text: Maintenance testing is not needed if the original tests passed

options.label: d
options.text: Maintenance testing must always include all previously executed test cases

a.explanation: Re-testing the entire scope would be impractical and unnecessary for most changes.

b.explanation: Maintenance testing scope is determined by impact analysis of the specific change. Only affected areas and potential regression risks need to be tested.

c.explanation: Maintenance testing is always needed to verify changes and check for regressions, even if the original tests passed.

d.explanation: Running all previously executed tests may be impractical and is not required; a targeted subset based on risk is more appropriate.

questions.questionText: Which of the following BEST describes DevOps from a testing perspective?

options.label: a
options.text: DevOps separates development and operations teams to improve specialization

options.label: b
options.text: DevOps promotes continuous testing integrated into the delivery pipeline to enable fast, frequent releases

options.label: c
options.text: DevOps replaces testing with peer code reviews

options.label: d
options.text: DevOps requires a dedicated testing phase between development and deployment

a.explanation: DevOps promotes collaboration and integration between development and operations teams, not separation.

b.explanation: DevOps integrates testing throughout the delivery pipeline (CI/CD), enabling fast and frequent releases with quality built in through continuous testing.

c.explanation: DevOps does not replace testing; it integrates it more deeply into the pipeline.

d.explanation: DevOps avoids discrete testing phases; testing is continuous and integrated throughout.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a defect type that static testing can detect but dynamic testing typically CANNOT?

options.label: a
options.text: A button that does not respond to mouse clicks

options.label: b
options.text: Inconsistencies or contradictions within a requirements document

options.label: c
options.text: A memory leak that occurs after hours of system operation

options.label: d
options.text: An error in a mathematical calculation in a report

a.explanation: A non-responsive button is detected through dynamic (UI) testing.

b.explanation: Reviews (static testing) of requirements documents can detect ambiguities, contradictions, and omissions that dynamic testing cannot address because the code may not yet exist.

c.explanation: Memory leaks are detected through dynamic performance or stress testing.

d.explanation: Calculation errors in reports are found by executing the report and comparing results — dynamic testing.

questions.questionText: Which of the following review types is primarily intended for knowledge transfer and training?

options.label: a
options.text: Inspection

options.label: b
options.text: Technical review

options.label: c
options.text: Walkthrough

options.label: d
options.text: Checklist-based review

a.explanation: Inspection is primarily for defect detection using a highly formal process.

b.explanation: Technical reviews focus on technical accuracy and consensus, not primarily on training.

c.explanation: Walkthroughs, led by the author, serve multiple purposes including knowledge sharing, training new team members, and gaining consensus, as well as finding defects.

d.explanation: Checklist-based review is a technique that can be applied within different review types, not a separate review type with a training focus.

questions.questionText: What is a key difference between a walkthrough and a technical review?

options.label: a
options.text: Only technical reviews find defects; walkthroughs do not

options.label: b
options.text: Walkthroughs are led by the author; technical reviews are led by a trained moderator or technical lead

options.label: c
options.text: Technical reviews are informal; walkthroughs are highly formal

options.label: d
options.text: Walkthroughs require a scribe; technical reviews do not

a.explanation: Both walkthroughs and technical reviews can find defects.

b.explanation: Walkthroughs are led by the author who presents the work product. Technical reviews are led by a trained moderator or senior technical person, making them more structured and objective.

c.explanation: Technical reviews are more formal than walkthroughs, not the other way around.

d.explanation: Scribes may be used in both types; this is not the key distinguishing factor.

questions.questionText: Which factor contributes to the SUCCESS of reviews?

options.label: a
options.text: Making review feedback personal and directed at the author rather than the work product

options.label: b
options.text: Having clear entry criteria for what work products can enter the review process

options.label: c
options.text: Allowing unlimited review scope to catch as many defects as possible

options.label: d
options.text: Limiting reviews to code only, excluding requirements and design documents

a.explanation: Making feedback personal undermines reviews; feedback should focus on the work product, not the author.

b.explanation: Clear entry criteria ensure that the work product is ready for review and that the review session is productive, contributing to review success.

c.explanation: Unlimited scope leads to unfocused, inefficient reviews; manageable scope is a success factor.

d.explanation: Reviews are beneficial for all types of work products, not just code.

questions.questionText: A function calculates a discount: 0% for purchases under $50, 5% for $50-$99, and 10% for $100 or more. Using equivalence partitioning, how many partitions exist in total (valid + invalid)?

a.explanation: There are 3 valid partitions alone, so the total cannot be 2.

b.explanation: 3 accounts only for the valid partitions; invalid partitions (negative amounts) should also be considered.

c.explanation: There are 3 valid partitions (under $50, $50-$99, $100+) and 1 invalid partition (negative values, e.g., -$1), giving 4 total partitions.

d.explanation: 5 partitions would require additional distinct behavior ranges not described in this scenario.

questions.questionText: Using boundary value analysis for a field that accepts ages from 0 to 120, which values should be tested using 2-value BVA?

a.explanation: This covers boundaries and midpoint but omits the values just outside the boundaries required by 2-value BVA.

b.explanation: 2-value BVA tests each boundary and its immediate neighbor outside the range. For 0-120: -1 (just below), 0 (lower boundary), 120 (upper boundary), 121 (just above).

c.explanation: Values 1 and 119 are inside the range; 2-value BVA requires values just outside the boundaries (-1 and 121), not just inside.

d.explanation: This tests values just outside AND just inside but misses the actual boundaries (0 and 120) which are essential in 2-value BVA.

questions.questionText: A system applies a late payment fee based on two conditions: whether the account is overdue (Yes/No) and whether the customer is a premium member (Yes/No). How many unique rules does a full decision table for this system have?

a.explanation: 2 would only cover one condition with two outcomes.

b.explanation: With 2 binary conditions, the full decision table has 2^2 = 4 rules: (Yes/Yes), (Yes/No), (No/Yes), (No/No).

c.explanation: 6 rules would require 3 binary conditions (2^3 would be 8, not 6).

d.explanation: 8 rules require 3 binary conditions; with only 2 conditions the answer is 4.

questions.questionText: In state transition testing, which coverage criterion requires that every valid transition is covered by at least one test case?

options.label: a
options.text: All-states coverage

options.label: b
options.text: All-transitions coverage

options.label: c
options.text: All-paths coverage

options.label: d
options.text: All-conditions coverage

a.explanation: All-states coverage only requires that every state is visited at least once, not every transition.

b.explanation: All-transitions coverage (transition coverage) requires that every valid transition in the state diagram is exercised by at least one test case.

c.explanation: All-paths coverage requires covering every unique path of transitions, which is more comprehensive and often impractical.

d.explanation: All-conditions coverage is a decision table or logic testing concept, not a standard state transition coverage criterion.

questions.questionText: A tester has written tests that achieve 80% statement coverage. What does this mean?

options.label: a
options.text: 80% of the requirements have been tested

options.label: b
options.text: 80% of the executable statements have been executed at least once

options.label: c
options.text: 80% of the test cases have passed

options.label: d
options.text: 80% of the defects have been found

a.explanation: Requirements coverage is a different metric from statement coverage.

b.explanation: Statement coverage percentage is the ratio of executed statements to total executable statements, so 80% means 80% of all executable statements have been run.

c.explanation: The pass rate of test cases is a different metric from code coverage.

d.explanation: Defect detection rate cannot be directly inferred from statement coverage.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a characteristic of checklist-based testing?

options.label: a
options.text: It uses the tester's intuition without any predefined guidance

options.label: b
options.text: It uses a prepared list of items derived from experience or standards to guide testing

options.label: c
options.text: It generates test cases algorithmically from formal specifications

options.label: d
options.text: It requires executing code with different input values to measure coverage

a.explanation: Checklist-based testing does use predefined guidance (the checklist) rather than pure intuition.

b.explanation: Checklist-based testing uses a prepared list of items (derived from experience, standards, or best practices) to ensure consistent coverage of important areas during testing.

c.explanation: Algorithmic test case generation from formal specifications describes model-based testing.

d.explanation: Measuring coverage through execution describes white-box testing.

questions.questionText: In Agile, what is the THREE AMIGOS technique used for?

options.label: a
options.text: A bug fixing process involving three developers

options.label: b
options.text: A collaborative session where a business analyst, developer, and tester discuss a user story to define acceptance criteria

options.label: c
options.text: A three-phase testing process: unit, integration, and system testing

options.label: d
options.text: A review process conducted by three independent testers

a.explanation: Three Amigos is not a bug-fixing process.

b.explanation: The Three Amigos technique involves a business analyst (or product owner), a developer, and a tester meeting to discuss a user story and define acceptance criteria collaboratively before implementation.

c.explanation: Test levels (unit, integration, system) are not the Three Amigos technique.

d.explanation: Three independent testers reviewing is a specific type of review activity, not the Three Amigos technique.

questions.questionText: Which test technique is BEST suited for testing the behavior of an online shopping system when a user adds an item to a cart, checks out, and then returns an item?

options.label: a
options.text: Equivalence partitioning

options.label: b
options.text: Boundary value analysis

options.label: c
options.text: State transition testing

options.label: d
options.text: Decision table testing

a.explanation: Equivalence partitioning is for input domain partitioning, not modeling multi-step workflows.

b.explanation: Boundary value analysis tests values at boundaries of ranges, not sequential state-based flows.

c.explanation: State transition testing is ideal for systems with distinct states (empty cart, cart with items, checked out, return initiated) and transitions between them triggered by events.

d.explanation: Decision table testing is for condition/action combinations, not sequential state-based navigation flows.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an ENTRY CRITERION that should typically be satisfied before starting test execution?

options.label: a
options.text: All planned test cases have been executed

options.label: b
options.text: The test environment has been set up and verified

options.label: c
options.text: All defects have been fixed and closed

options.label: d
options.text: The test completion report has been approved

a.explanation: Executing all test cases is an exit criterion, not an entry criterion.

b.explanation: Having the test environment set up and verified is an entry criterion — a condition that should be met before test execution can begin productively.

c.explanation: Requiring all defects to be fixed before execution would be impractical and is an exit criterion, not entry criterion.

d.explanation: The test completion report is produced after execution; it cannot be an entry criterion.

questions.questionText: How does risk-based testing affect the order in which tests are prioritized and executed?

options.label: a
options.text: Tests are executed alphabetically by test case name

options.label: b
options.text: Tests covering higher-risk areas are executed first to detect critical issues early

options.label: c
options.text: Tests with the lowest effort are always executed before higher-effort tests

options.label: d
options.text: Test execution order is determined by the development team, not the test team

a.explanation: Alphabetical ordering ignores risk and business value.

b.explanation: Risk-based testing prioritizes tests covering the highest-risk features first so that critical issues are found early, while lower-risk areas may be tested last or with less depth if time is short.

c.explanation: Effort alone does not determine execution order in risk-based testing.

d.explanation: Test execution order is decided by the test team based on risk analysis.

questions.questionText: Which estimation approach relies on gathering estimates from multiple experts independently and then reaching consensus?

options.label: a
options.text: Metric-based estimation

options.label: b
options.text: Expert-based estimation using Wideband Delphi

options.label: c
options.text: Bottom-up estimation

options.label: d
options.text: Parametric estimation

a.explanation: Metric-based estimation uses historical data, not individual expert estimates and consensus.

b.explanation: Wideband Delphi is a consensus-based expert estimation technique where experts provide estimates independently (to avoid anchoring bias), then discuss and converge on a final estimate.

c.explanation: Bottom-up estimation decomposes work into smaller items and sums estimates, but is not specifically a consensus technique.

d.explanation: Parametric estimation uses mathematical models, not expert consensus.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an EXIT CRITERION for test execution?

options.label: a
options.text: Test cases have been designed and reviewed

options.label: b
options.text: The test environment is available and configured

options.label: c
options.text: A specified percentage of test cases have been executed with acceptable results

options.label: d
options.text: The test plan has been approved by management

a.explanation: Test cases being designed and reviewed is an entry criterion for test execution, not an exit criterion.

b.explanation: Test environment availability is an entry criterion.

c.explanation: Exit criteria for test execution typically include conditions such as a specified percentage of test cases executed and passed, and defect rate below a threshold.

d.explanation: Test plan approval is an entry criterion for the testing project, not an exit criterion for test execution.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is included in a TEST COMPLETION report but NOT typically in a test progress report?

options.label: a
options.text: Current count of open defects

options.label: b
options.text: Number of test cases executed so far

options.label: c
options.text: Lessons learned and recommendations for future projects

options.label: d
options.text: Current test schedule status

a.explanation: Open defect counts appear in both progress and completion reports.

b.explanation: Test execution counts are in progress reports during testing.

c.explanation: Lessons learned and future recommendations are a key component of the test completion report, produced at the end. Progress reports provide current status, not retrospective insights.

d.explanation: Schedule status is reported in progress reports.

questions.questionText: In the context of ISTQB CTFL v4.0, what is a 'baseline' in configuration management?

options.label: a
options.text: The minimum acceptable quality level for a release

options.label: b
options.text: A formally approved version of one or more work products that serves as the basis for further work

options.label: c
options.text: The initial set of requirements before any changes are made

options.label: d
options.text: The performance benchmark against which the system is compared

a.explanation: Minimum quality level is a quality threshold, not a configuration management baseline.

b.explanation: A baseline is a formally approved snapshot of one or more work products at a specific point in time, which is then placed under change control and serves as the starting point for subsequent work.

c.explanation: While original requirements may form a baseline, the term 'baseline' applies to any formally approved version of work products, not just requirements.

d.explanation: Performance benchmarks are performance testing artifacts, not configuration management baselines.

questions.questionText: A tester discovers a defect that crashes the entire application, but it only occurs in a scenario used by less than 0.1% of users. How should severity and priority likely be set?

options.label: a
options.text: High severity, high priority

options.label: b
options.text: High severity, low priority

options.label: c
options.text: Low severity, high priority

options.label: d
options.text: Low severity, low priority

a.explanation: While severity is high (crash), priority would typically be low due to extremely rare occurrence.

b.explanation: The defect causes an application crash (high severity), but since it affects only 0.1% of users, the business priority for fixing it may be relatively low compared to other issues.

c.explanation: An application crash is always high severity; low severity would apply to minor cosmetic issues.

d.explanation: A crash is high severity by definition; this combination is incorrect.

questions.questionText: What is the purpose of 'defect clustering' information in risk-based testing?

options.label: a
options.text: To determine the total number of defects in the system

options.label: b
options.text: To focus testing effort on modules that have historically contained the most defects

options.label: c
options.text: To decide when to stop testing

options.label: d
options.text: To prioritize defect fixes over new feature development

a.explanation: Defect clustering informs testing focus, not the total defect count.

b.explanation: Knowledge of defect clustering helps testers focus effort on high-defect-density modules, which are more likely to have additional defects due to their complexity or historical error rates.

c.explanation: Stopping decisions are based on exit criteria, not defect clustering alone.

d.explanation: Prioritizing fixes vs. new features is a management decision, not what defect clustering is used for in testing.

questions.questionText: Which of the following BEST describes how testing contributes to quality in the SDLC?

options.label: a
options.text: Testing adds quality to the software by fixing the defects it finds

options.label: b
options.text: Testing provides information about the quality of the software to help stakeholders make informed decisions

options.label: c
options.text: Testing removes all defects from the software before release

options.label: d
options.text: Testing produces the software requirements that guide development

a.explanation: Testers find and report defects; developers fix them. Testing itself does not fix defects.

b.explanation: Testing provides information about the quality status of the software, which enables stakeholders to make informed decisions about releases, further development, and risk management.

c.explanation: Testing cannot remove all defects; it reduces the risk of defects remaining undetected.

d.explanation: Requirements are produced by business analysts and product owners, not by testing.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a KEY factor to consider when deciding whether to automate a test?

options.label: a
options.text: Whether the test was written by a developer or a tester

options.label: b
options.text: Whether the test is repeatable and stable enough to justify the automation investment

options.label: c
options.text: Whether the test is for functional or non-functional requirements

options.label: d
options.text: Whether the test is listed in the test plan

a.explanation: Authorship does not determine automation suitability.

b.explanation: Tests that are executed frequently (repeatable) and involve stable features provide the best return on automation investment, justifying the initial cost of automation.

c.explanation: Both functional and non-functional tests can be automated; the type alone does not determine suitability.

d.explanation: Being listed in the test plan does not determine automation suitability.

questions.questionText: What is meant by 'false confidence' as a risk of test automation?

options.label: a
options.text: Believing automated tests are slower than manual tests

options.label: b
options.text: Assuming that passing automated tests means the software has no defects

options.label: c
options.text: Trusting that automation tools will never produce incorrect results

options.label: d
options.text: Believing that test automation costs nothing to maintain

a.explanation: Speed comparison is not what false confidence means in this context.

b.explanation: False confidence occurs when teams assume that all-green automated test results mean the software is defect-free, ignoring areas not covered by automation or issues automation cannot detect.

c.explanation: Tool accuracy is a separate concern from false confidence in test outcomes.

d.explanation: Underestimating maintenance cost is a different automation risk, not false confidence.

questions.questionText: Which tool category would BEST support a team that needs to track which test cases cover which requirements?

options.label: a
options.text: Performance testing tool

options.label: b
options.text: Test management tool with traceability features

options.label: c
options.text: Static analysis tool

options.label: d
options.text: Defect simulation tool

a.explanation: Performance tools measure system performance under load, not requirements traceability.

b.explanation: Test management tools with traceability features maintain bidirectional links between requirements and test cases, showing coverage and gaps.

c.explanation: Static analysis tools examine code quality; they do not manage test-to-requirement traceability.

d.explanation: Defect simulation tools are not a standard category and do not support requirements traceability.

questions.questionText: A module has the following code structure: one IF statement with a true branch containing 3 statements and a false branch containing 2 statements. What is the minimum number of test cases needed to achieve 100% branch coverage?

a.explanation: One test case can only take either the true or false branch, not both.

b.explanation: Branch coverage requires both the true and false outcomes of the IF statement to be tested. Minimum 2 test cases: one that makes the condition true, one that makes it false.

c.explanation: 5 matches the total number of statements, which relates to statement coverage counting, not the minimum test cases for branch coverage.

d.explanation: 6 would over-cover; only 2 test cases are needed for branch coverage of a single decision.

questions.questionText: Which of the following BEST distinguishes a test condition from a test case?

options.label: a
options.text: A test condition is a testable aspect of the system; a test case is a set of inputs, execution conditions, and expected results to verify a test condition

options.label: b
options.text: A test case is more abstract than a test condition

options.label: c
options.text: Test conditions are produced during test execution; test cases are produced during test planning

options.label: d
options.text: A test condition specifies the exact steps to run a test; a test case specifies the area to be tested

a.explanation: A test condition is a testable aspect, item, or characteristic of the system. A test case is a concrete specification with inputs, execution preconditions, and expected results designed to verify that condition.

b.explanation: It is the other way around: test conditions are more abstract; test cases are more specific and concrete.

c.explanation: Test conditions are derived during test analysis; test cases are designed during test design — both before execution.

d.explanation: This reverses the definitions; test cases specify exact steps while test conditions identify what needs to be tested.
